body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the 81 live gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket — a genuinely quiet day, not a data gap. That's not surprising given how the two boards are priced: Kalshi's September 30, 2026 settlement ladder crosses 50/50 between the $4,330.99 strike (bid 53¢/ask 57¢) and the $4,370.99 strike (bid 46¢/ask 49¢), implying the market sees spot gold sitting right around $4,350 today. That lines up with independent price data showing gold trading near $4,385–$4,406 in the first half of September 2026 (USAGold, Traders Agency), so the two prediction markets and the underlying spot market are telling a consistent story.

The bigger context for readers new to the space: gold has been extraordinarily volatile this year. Gold's all-time high is $5,589.38 per ounce, reached on January 28, 2026. It has since pulled back sharply, and current commentary points to gold starting the week near $4,410 after ending last week around $4,429, with strong U.S. job growth increasing expectations of a rate hike in September — an unusual dynamic since gold typically dislikes rate hikes. That backdrop explains why Polymarket's touch contracts for round numbers like $4,300 and $4,400 in September are priced high (77¢ and 81¢ respectively): those are contracts that pay out if the price ever crossed the line during the month, not where it settled, so a choppy month makes both a dip and a spike easy to satisfy.

One mechanical note worth flagging: several Polymarket weekly contracts (e.g., the Week of September 14 touch markets) are quoting bid 2¢ / ask 98¢. That's not a real price signal — it's an empty or near-empty order book, and any scanner should ignore spreads that wide as tradeable edge rather than a hint of mispricing.
headline: No arbitrage across 81 gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket as prices align
